content:
Priya Shah: Hey @eng-platform quick question from triage — can rate-limit headers become inconsistent when fallback routing kicks in?

We’re seeing a few tickets where customer claims limit is X in `x-ratelimit-limit-requests` but then they get 429s way sooner, and the headers on retries don’t line up (`remaining` jumps around). Trying to decide if this is “expected under fallback” vs a bug.

Context:
- Similar to SUP-1843 / SUP-1855 (post-SDK upgrade + header confusion)
- Some of these correlate with elevated fallback (routing) in the last hour

Dashboards:
- Routing fallback overview: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/routing-fallback/overview?orgId=1
- Rate limit service errors: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quota-rl/quota-rate-limit?orgId=1
- Gateway 429 breakdown: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/gw-errors/gateway-errors?orgId=1&var-code=429

If it can happen, what’s the right guidance for Support? (e.g., “headers are best-effort during incident/fallback; rely on request_id + we can verify limits internally”).

Owen Phillips: +1, I’m writing an internal macro and don’t want to promise headers are always authoritative if they’re not. :grimacing:

Ethan Park: looping in @Mina Haddad as well (routing/fallback). I can give initial take but Mina will have the exact behavior.

Ethan Park: Short answer: it *can* look inconsistent under certain fallback paths.

Longer: the gateway generates headers based on the quota decision it has for the specific upstream pool. If a request gets routed to a different pool/region (fallback), the limits/remaining you see can reflect a different quota shard/state than the previous request.

It shouldn’t be wildly wrong, but “remaining jumps” is something we’ve seen when:
1) fallback flips between pools within a short window, and
2) the client is doing concurrent requests + retries (so ordering isn’t what they assume)

We have a fix in flight to make headers more consistent (ENG-4825 / PR-19322). Still validating.

Mina Haddad: Yep confirming. Under fallback we can route across capacity tiers / pools, and the quota decision can be evaluated against different enforcement points depending on where the request lands.

What’s *expected* today:
- Headers are accurate *for that request* but not guaranteed to be monotonic across retries if routing changes.
- `remaining` can increase on a subsequent request if it went to a different pool or if the earlier request’s quota state hasn’t propagated yet.
- In fail-open scenarios (rare), you might see headers that look permissive but enforcement happens downstream.

What’s *not expected*:
- Same request_id returning multiple different limit values (unless the client is re-sending and getting a new request_id each time).

Benji Okafor: Also note some SDKs log `x-request-id` but customers paste `cf-ray`/proxy ids instead. If you can get the Redwood request ID we can look up the actual enforcement decision.

Priya Shah: Super helpful. Is there a metric we can check quickly to tell if fallback was active for a specific time window? (so we can say “this likely explains the header mismatch”).

Mina Haddad: Use the fallback overlay on the routing dashboard and the per-route metric:
- `routing_fallback_active{route=...,region=...}`
- `routing_fallback_reason{reason=capacity|health|policy}`

We’re adding a clearer Support-friendly panel soon (ENG-4821) because right now it’s a bit too “eng-y”.

Link for now (filtered view): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/routing-fallback/overview?orgId=1&var-region=us-east&viewPanel=12

Dev Patel: For Support guidance, can we state something like:
“During fallback or incident mitigation, rate-limit headers may not be consistent across retries. Treat 429 as authoritative, and share request IDs so we can confirm quota + routing on our side.”

Ethan Park: Yes, that wording is fine.

Suggested Support-safe guidance:
- Don’t tell customers to build strict logic off `remaining` being monotonic.
- Recommend honoring 429 with exponential backoff + jitter.
- If they need exact quota info, point them to Console usage view (or we can confirm internally).

Also: if they’re on streaming, retries can multiply apparent usage; worth checking they’re not auto-retrying without idempotency.

Owen Phillips: Great. I’ll update the macro + link the KB draft for 429/quota mismatch. Mina/Ethan if you want to add a 1-2 sentence “fallback note” to the article, I’ll pull it in.

Mina Haddad: Please do. Keep it generic (no internal architecture details). Something like: “If the platform is routing requests to alternate capacity (fallback), headers may vary between requests.”

Priya Shah: Cool, I’ll add that note to the draft and tag you both for quick review. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

(reactions: Ethan Park :thumbsup:, Mina Haddad :white_check_mark:)
